speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. Can you describe the nature of the pain in your left shoulder, such as whether it is sharp, dull, or burning, and when it typically occurs?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes and the specific difficulty with overhead movements like brushing your hair, I need to assess your range of motion more closely. Is the limitation in your shoulder movement due to pain, or does the joint feel mechanically blocked from moving further?

speaker: Doctor
text: The restriction appears to be a mechanical "freezing" rather than just pain limitation, which strongly suggests adhesive capsulitis given your diabetes. Do you experience significantly more pain when I passively move your arm versus when you try to move it yourself?

The X-ray will help rule out osteoarthritis or calcific tendinitis, which are important differentials in a diabetic patient with shoulder pain.

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal X-ray rules out bony pathology, which, combined with your diabetes and the global restriction of both active and passive motion, strongly points to adhesive capsulitis. I would like to see clinical images of your shoulder range of motion to confirm the characteristic capsular pattern of restriction. REQUEST IMAGES
